subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: GPS: Engineering Precision from Space
description: A quick, practical guide to GPS: Engineering Precision from Space.

hook.text: GPS can pinpoint your location to within 30 centimeters. It uses satellites orbiting at 20,200 km altitude.

buildup.text: Your phone receives signals from at least four satellites. It calculates distance from each one's time delay.

discovery.text: GPS clocks must be accurate to billionths of a second. A one-microsecond error means 300 meters off.

twist.text: Einstein's relativity matters. Satellite clocks tick 38 microseconds faster per day due to weaker gravity.

climax.text: Without a relativity correction, GPS would drift 10 kilometers per day. Physics saves navigation.

punchline.text: Your map app runs on Einstein's equations.

quiz.question: Why does GPS require corrections based on Einstein's relativity?
options: Satellites move so fast their signals get Doppler-shifted
Satellite clocks tick faster due to weaker gravity in orbit
Radio waves bend around the Earth's magnetic field
